scopeNote: The frozen holdout fixtures (tests/fixtures/unseen-packages/final-phase3-closure-holdout-run/holdout-*.json) preserve { region, operativeSourceText, compile: {status, rules, definitions, failureReasons, telemetry}, verify }. rawModelOutput and toolCallLog were NOT preserved to disk during the prior run. Every row below is built from: (1) the real, structured post-normalization compile output including each definition's calculationExpression.kind/reason/sufficiency fields (which are themselves precise, machine-generated diagnostic strings, not paraphrased); (2) the independent verifier's own findings, which quote and analyze real source text; (3) direct comparison against the real, unmodified operativeSourceText already present in each fixture; (4) direct reading of the exact production code paths (lib/contract-model/ir/type-check.ts, lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/normalize.ts) that produced each reason string, confirmed line-by-line. This substitutes for raw model output honestly rather than presenting it as available.

compiledCalculationExpression.reason: ADD operands do not type-check together under the IR's own composition rules

rows.codePathConfirmed: normalize.ts:159-169 recursively normalizes each ADD operand into a full IRExpression subtree first (line 168), then buildComposite (normalize.ts:94-99) calls inferType(draft) on the assembled composite; type-check.ts:42-55's ADD/SUM rule propagates UNSUPPORTED_TYPE the moment ANY operand isUnsupported (line 45). Because the definition's own clause (2) cross-reference could not be resolved (see sufficiencyReasons in the fixture), at least one of the ~20 addback/subtraction operands normalized to an UNSUPPORTED leaf, poisoning inferType's verdict for the WHOLE ADD node - and buildComposite (normalize.ts:97) then DISCARDS the entire assembled operands array (including the ~15+ successfully-typed sibling addback clauses) and replaces the whole tree with one flat, structureless UNSUPPORTED leaf.
rows.evidenceModelDidDecompose: definition.dependsOnTerms lists 9 real, correctly-identified dependency terms (Consolidated Net Income, Consolidated Interest Expense, Consolidated Depreciation and Amortization Expense, Transaction Expenses, Permitted Acquisition, Disqualified Stock, Equity Interests, Closing Date, Borrower) and sufficiencyReasons narrates real per-clause analysis (clause (1)(g) correctly recognized as '[reserved]' and omitted; clause (1)(l)'s run-rate formula correctly captured; clause (2)'s cross-reference correctly flagged unresolved) - the model DID attempt full decomposition; the loss happens in deterministic post-processing, not model reasoning.
rows.evidenceNotTokenLimited: outputTokens=17853 of a 128000 cap; attemptCount=6 of a maxToolCalls=8 budget - nowhere near either limit.

rows.definitionOrTermExamined: Consolidated First Lien Secured Debt (UNSUPPORTED, distinct root cause) + Consolidated Interest Expense (UNSUPPORTED, same ADD poison-propagation defect as A1/A2)

compiledCalculationExpression.reason: First Lien Secured Debt: 'This is a categorical inclusion/exclusion filter applied to a stock variable (outstanding Indebtedness), including a nested carve-back exception...There is no FILTER/categorical-set primitive in the available node kinds to express...forcing this into ADD/SUBTRACT/SUM over METRIC_REFERENCE nodes would fabricate a false arithmetic decomposition of what is really a scope/eligibility test, not a formula over known numeric metrics.'; Interest Expense: 'ADD operands do not type-check together under the IR's own composition rules'

rows.codePathConfirmed: Consolidated First Lien Secured Debt's own reason string is NOT a type-check poison-propagation symptom - it is the model correctly and explicitly declining to fabricate a false arithmetic decomposition because the IR's expression vocabulary (types.ts) has no node kind representing 'the set of Indebtedness instruments meeting inclusion criteria X/Y/Z minus exclusion criteria D/E/F, with a nested carve-back re-inclusion for G' - a categorical eligibility/scope test over a set of legal instruments, structurally different from a formula over known scalar metrics. This is a genuine, narrow IR-expressivity gap, distinct from the buildComposite defect seen elsewhere in this ledger.
rows.evidenceModelDidDecompose: The model's own reasoning explicitly names the missing primitive and explains why forcing existing nodes would be dishonest - this is a correct, well-reasoned UNSUPPORTED, not a decomposition failure.
rows.outcome: SUBSTANTIVE_MISS_SAFELY_SURFACED (verify status VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE). IMPORTANT: this specific narrow IR-expressivity gap (categorical inclusion/exclusion filter over a set of debt instruments) is NOT one of the mission's own A-J synthetic representability test scenarios (see 02-ir-representability-analysis.json) and is NOT remediated by this mission's bounded fix - it is disclosed honestly as an out-of-scope residual limitation. The mission's own semantic pass gate tolerates up to 1 safely-surfaced miss among A1-A6; if A4's Consolidated First Lien Secured Debt sub-claim is the GT target, it may remain the 1 acceptable miss after remediation.

compiledCalculationExpression.reason: DURING_PERIOD value type could not be determined

rows.codePathConfirmed: normalize.ts:210-213 (DURING_PERIOD branch) wraps a normalized child value node; type-check.ts:129-132's DURING_PERIOD rule simply forwards the child's inferred type (t = inferType(expr.value); return t). If the wrapped value itself is UNSUPPORTED (e.g. because IT is a composite poisoned by the SAME buildComposite defect as A1/A2), DURING_PERIOD inherits UNSUPPORTED and buildComposite (normalize.ts:213, unsupportedMessage 'DURING_PERIOD value type could not be determined') again discards the wrapped structure. Same underlying defect class, one level of wrapping deeper.

compiledCalculationExpression.reason: IF condition must be BOOLEAN and both branches must resolve to the same type

rows.codePathConfirmed: normalize.ts:195-200 (IF branch) recursively normalizes condition/then/else, then buildComposite/type-check.ts:116-124's IF rule poisons if the condition is not BOOLEAN OR the two branches' types diverge. A multi-tier pricing grid re-expressed as nested IF/IF/IF (rather than the IR's own purpose-built SCHEDULE node, which exists precisely for tiered thresholds) is a well-known shape mismatch risk: if the model nested nine leverage-ratio tiers as chained IFs where an intermediate branch itself ended up UNSUPPORTED (e.g., a further nested composite also poisoned), the whole tree collapses to one flat leaf - same defect class as A1/A2/A5/A6, manifesting through IF instead of ADD/SUBTRACT/DURING_PERIOD. The verifier's 27 real findings (10+ MISSING_BASKET quoting exact real percentages/breakpoints: 8.00%, 7.00%, 7.75%, 6.75%, 7.50%, 6.50%, 1.00-to-1.00, 0.50-to-1.00) confirm real, itemizable structure existed in the source that the compiled IF/UNSUPPORTED collapse lost.
rows.evidenceModelDidDecompose: The verifier's itemized findings quoting exact real numeric values from the source indicate the source structure is well-defined; the compiler attempted an IF-based decomposition (per the reason string referencing 'IF condition' and 'both branches') rather than failing outright.
rows.evidenceNotTokenLimited: outputTokens=21229 of 128000 (shared with B1); attemptCount=2 of 8.
rows.outcome: QUALIFIER_MISS_SAFELY_SURFACED_WITH_DETAILED_ITEMIZATION. Separately notable: SCHEDULE is the IR's purpose-built node for tiered pricing grids (types.ts) but the model reached for IF instead - a possible PROMPT_INSTRUCTION opportunity (lightly clarify SCHEDULE's applicability for pricing-grid shapes) but NOT a required fix, since the buildComposite preservation fix (04) benefits IF-based decompositions equally without needing to force SCHEDULE specifically.

aggregateFindings.dominantFailureLayer: NORMALIZATION - the buildComposite/inferType poison-propagation discard pattern accounts for the calculationExpression-level failure in at least 6 of the 10 claims (A1, A2, A5, A6/Maintenance-Liquidity, B2, B3) and appears across FOUR distinct composite kinds (ADD, SUBTRACT, IF, DURING_PERIOD-wrapping-a-poisoned-child), confirming the defect is generic to the composite-assembly mechanism, not specific to any one operator or to EBITDA specifically.
aggregateFindings.secondaryFailureLayer: SOURCE_CONTEXT - 2 claims (A3/Consolidated Maintenance EBITDA, A6/Invoice Restrictions) show a genuine, correctly self-reported region/document-scoping limitation unrelated to semantic-computation architecture; these are NOT fixed by Unit A and are honestly excluded from its remediation scope.
aggregateFindings.narrowExpressivityGap: 1 claim (A4/Consolidated First Lien Secured Debt) shows a genuine, narrow IR-expressivity gap for categorical inclusion/exclusion filters over a set of legal instruments - distinct from the dominant poison-propagation defect, not covered by the mission's own A-J synthetic representability test set (see 02), and NOT remediated by this mission's bounded fix (see 04's explicit scope boundary).
aggregateFindings.positiveControlEvidence: B1 (Applicable Liquidity Threshold, IF) and B4 (both cash-sweep-cure definitions, ADD/MIN/SUBTRACT) demonstrate the compilation architecture DOES produce real, deterministically-executable structure when a composite's operands genuinely type-check - the defect is specifically the DISCARD behavior on partial failure, not a universal inability to compute.
aggregateFindings.noEvidenceOfTokenOrToolBudgetLimiting: Every claim's outputTokens is well under the 128000 cap (range 7488-21229) and attemptCount is well under the 8-call budget (range 1-6) - ruling out 'increase model output tokens' as a fix, per the mission's own explicit prohibition.
aggregateFindings.noEvidenceOfModelDecompositionFailure: In every row where the underlying source was fully in scope, the model's own dependsOnTerms/sufficiencyReasons/definition counts demonstrate real, correct, fine-grained decomposition attempts - the loss occurs in deterministic post-processing (buildComposite), not in the model's reasoning.
